title: Google Maps can now build trip itineraries with real-time details about each stop
slides: Google Maps now plans trips. But can you trust it?
Itineraries include live hours, traffic, and closures per stop
The plan rewrites itself mid-trip when conditions change
You can skip manual research for multi-stop day trips
Test it on one weekend trip before relying on it
thread_text:
1. The 20-minute trap

Google Maps now builds multi-stop itineraries with live hours, traffic, and closures. The catch: you're trusting an algorithm with your entire day.

2. Plans that rewrite themselves

Mid-trip, the itinerary updates when a stop closes or traffic spikes. No manual re-planning — but you lose control over what changes.

3. Skip the research rabbit hole

No more cross-checking hours across five tabs. The plan pulls everything into one timeline, so you just follow it.

4. The real risk is hidden

One wrong closure or outdated hour and your whole chain collapses. The algorithm won't warn you — it just reroutes.

5. Test before you trust

Use it on one weekend trip first. If the plan holds without edits, scale up. If not, you know the limit.

instagram.caption:
Google Maps now builds multi-stop itineraries that update themselves mid-trip when a stop closes or traffic spikes. 🗺️

Live hours, closures and traffic get pulled into one timeline, so you follow it instead of cross-checking five tabs.

The risk sits underneath: one outdated closure and the whole chain collapses — the algorithm won't warn you, it just reroutes. ⚠️

For anyone planning shoots, meetings or content days across town, that means less research time but a quiet loss of control over what changes.

Run it on one weekend trip first. 🚗 If the plan holds without edits, scale up. If not, you've found its limit.
